previous_headings: Common pitfalls
what: Pitfall 1: The intercept is not “the average response”
title: Reading factors, dummies, and interactions
text: Symptom. reviewer asks intercept means; author answers “average body mass”. number way compared mean(dat$body_mass), now everyone confused. Diagnosis. body_mass ~ sex + body_size, intercept expected response reference level every factor zero every continuous predictor. fit sex = factor(female, male) means “expected body_mass FEMALE body_size = 0”. overall mean unless sexes balanced body_size already centred zero. Rule thumb. Read intercept expected response reference factor level zero every continuous predictor.
code: n_p1 <- 80 sex_p1 <- factor(sample(c("female", "male"), n_p1, replace = TRUE)) bs_p1  <- runif(n_p1, 50, 150) dat_p1 <- data.frame(   body_mass = rnorm(n_p1, 30 + 5 * (sex_p1 == "male") + 0.2 * bs_p1, 3),   sex       = sex_p1,   body_size = bs_p1 ) fit_p1 <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ sex + body_size, sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p1 ) sym_p1 <- symbolize(fit_p1, context = "intercept reading")  # WRONG: read the intercept as the grand mean. #   "the average body mass is 12.0 g" -- it is not. # RIGHT: read the intercept as the reference cell. #   symbol_table() flags the reference level so this is auditable. symbol_table(sym_p1)

what: Pitfall 2: A factor contrast is not the group’s mean
title: Reading factors, dummies, and interactions
text: Symptom. paper sentence says “male body mass 5 g (sexmale coefficient)”. reader checks mean(body_mass[sex == "male"]) gets ~35 g. sentence wrong. Diagnosis. sexmale coefficient difference male female cell means, male mean. male mean (Intercept) + sexmale. group_means(sym, = "sex") returns cell mean directly confidence band, readers actually wanted. Group means Rows marked * 95% confidence interval excludes zero (CI method: wald). Rule thumb. Coefficients factor levels differences reference; use group_means(sym) see group means .
code: n_p2 <- 80 sex_p2 <- factor(sample(c("female", "male"), n_p2, replace = TRUE)) dat_p2 <- data.frame(   body_mass = rnorm(n_p2, 30 + 5 * (sex_p2 == "male"), 3),   sex       = sex_p2 ) fit_p2 <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ sex, sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p2 ) sym_p2 <- symbolize(fit_p2, context = "contrast vs cell mean")  # WRONG: read the sexmale coefficient as the male mean. sym_p2$fixed_effects[, c("term_label", "estimate")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   term_label  estimate #>   <chr>          <dbl> #> 1 (Intercept)    30.0  #> 2 sex             5.35 #> 3 (Intercept)     1.02  # RIGHT: ask for the cell means directly. group_means(sym_p2, by = "sex")

what: Pitfall 3: An interaction is not “the effect of A on B”
title: Reading factors, dummies, and interactions
text: Symptom. methods section says “interaction tests whether sex effect body size”. category error — sex effect body size; interaction tests whether slope one predictor depends level . Diagnosis. body_mass ~ sex * body_size, sexmale:body_size coefficient difference male female slopes body_size, “effect sex body_size”. honest reading “slope body_size X females X + Y males”. group_slopes(sym, continuous = "body_size") returns per-group slopes directly. Group slopes body_size Rows marked * 95% confidence interval excludes zero (CI method: wald). Rule thumb. interaction coefficient difference two effects, either effect alone; use group_slopes(sym, continuous = ...) read group’s slope.
code: n_p3 <- 80 sex_p3 <- factor(sample(c("female", "male"), n_p3, replace = TRUE)) bs_p3  <- runif(n_p3, 50, 150) dat_p3 <- data.frame(   body_mass = rnorm(     n_p3,     30 + 5 * (sex_p3 == "male") + 0.2 * bs_p3 +       0.05 * (sex_p3 == "male") * bs_p3,     3   ),   sex       = sex_p3,   body_size = bs_p3 ) fit_p3 <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ sex * body_size, sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p3 ) sym_p3 <- symbolize(fit_p3, context = "interaction wording")  # WRONG: "the sexmale:body_size coefficient is the effect of sex on body_size." # RIGHT: it is the difference in body_size slopes between male and female. group_slopes(sym_p3, continuous = "body_size")

what: Pitfall 4: Wald CIs can be too narrow with few groups
title: Reading factors, dummies, and interactions
text: Symptom. fit (1 | site) six sites reports tight confidence bands fixed effects. bands look precise data justify, reviewer asks computed. Diagnosis. drmTMB’s default ci_method = "wald", uses asymptotic normal approximation. sd(site) estimated handful groups, asymptotic regime kicked , Wald intervals -state precision. Profile-likelihood intervals honest slower compute. flag lives symbolize() choice recorded x$metadata$ci_method propagates every downstream reading. Rule thumb. sd(group) estimated groups, pass ci_method = "profile" symbolize() honest interval.
code: # WRONG: take the default Wald CI when only a few groups inform sd(site). sym_wald <- symbolize(fit, ci_method = "wald")  # RIGHT: ask for a profile CI — slower, but honest. sym_prof <- symbolize(fit, ci_method = "profile")

what: Pitfall 5: Dropping the intercept doesn’t always do what you think
title: Reading factors, dummies, and interactions
text: Symptom. user wants every cell mean directly, types y ~ 0 + sex + site thinking give sex × site cell means, surprised coefficients still look like contrasts. Diagnosis. y ~ 0 + sex one factor give cell means directly (one coefficient per level). adding second predictor, e.g. y ~ 0 + sex + site, gives “sex cell means PLUS site contrasts reference site”. non-orthogonality two factors without intercept rarely reader wanted. group_means(sym, = c("sex", "site")) returns every cell mean correctly regardless formula written. Group means Rows marked * 95% confidence interval excludes zero (CI method: wald). Rule thumb. two factors, safest way get cell means group_means(sym, = c(...)), hand-built intercept-less formula.
code: n_p5 <- 100 sex_p5  <- factor(sample(c("female", "male"), n_p5, replace = TRUE)) site_p5 <- factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n_p5, replace = TRUE)) dat_p5 <- data.frame(   body_mass = rnorm(n_p5, 30 + 5 * (sex_p5 == "male"), 3),   sex       = sex_p5,   site      = site_p5 )  # WRONG: drop the intercept and hope to read all 6 cell means off the table. fit_p5_wrong <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ 0 + sex + site, sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p5 )  # RIGHT: keep the intercept in, fit ~ sex * site, then use group_means(). fit_p5_right <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ sex * site, sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p5 ) sym_p5 <- symbolize(fit_p5_right, context = "all cell means") group_means(sym_p5, by = c("sex", "site"))

what: Pitfall 6: poly(x, 2) and I(x^2) are not the same
title: Reading factors, dummies, and interactions
text: Symptom. paper reports “slope body_size 0.18 g/mm (poly(body_size, 2)1 coefficient)”. number happens match expected linear slope, looks fine — column first orthogonal polynomial body_size, raw linear term. Diagnosis. poly(x, 2) produces two ORTHOGONAL columns: combination xx x2x^2 scaled two columns uncorrelated. first column “slope xx”. contrast (x^2) puts literal x2x^2 column design matrix alongside separate linear xx term, now linear coefficient slope x=0x = 0. two parameterisations carry information coefficient interpretations differ. Use whichever fits story. Rule thumb. Use poly(x, 2) want orthogonal columns (uncorrelated polynomial terms); use (x^2) want literal quadratic interpretation.
code: n_p6 <- 80 bs_p6 <- runif(n_p6, -1, 1) dat_p6 <- data.frame(   body_mass = rnorm(n_p6, 30 + 0.2 * bs_p6 + 0.5 * bs_p6^2, 1),   body_size = bs_p6 )  # WRONG: read the poly() column as a literal linear slope. fit_p6_poly <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ poly(body_size, 2), sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p6 ) sym_p6_poly <- symbolize(fit_p6_poly, context = "orthogonal polynomial")  # RIGHT: use I(x^2) when you want a literal quadratic reading. fit_p6_raw <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ body_size + I(body_size^2), sigma ~ 1),   family = gaussian(), data = dat_p6 ) sym_p6_raw <- symbolize(fit_p6_raw, context = "raw quadratic")  symbol_table(sym_p6_poly) symbol_table(sym_p6_raw)
